description: Set a shot's camera (shot_id, or scene + shot; left out: the shot on screen): a preset move with strength and wiggle, or direct it with camera keys (keys win over the move). Each key: at (seconds) and any of x, y, z, distance, height, angle, roll, ease; what a key leaves out is taken from where the camera is at that moment. Ids must come from the current style: call library to see them (a wrong id is refused with the valid list). Returns the camera settings. One undo step for the person. For the end-of-shot camera move into the next shot, use set_transition (outro_camera).

clear_keys.description: true: drop camera keys, back to the move.

distance.description: Distance from that point, about 2 to 40.

ease.description: smooth, even, fast-start, slow-start, punch, bounce

roll.description: Tilt of the picture, about -3.2 to 3.2.

still.description: true on a single key: a locked camera that doesn't move.

z.description: Point it looks at: near (+) / far (-).

move.description: Camera move id (library cameras). Clears camera keys.

replace_keys.description: false: add these keys to the ones there. Default replaces them.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

strength.description: How far the move goes, 0 to 100.

wiggle.description: Handheld feel: 0 locked off, 1 normal, up to 3.

name: set_camera
